Really gorgeous little game. I had it in my library for ages, and I'm really glad I finally picked it up. The gameplay style and dark folklore tone reminded me a bit of Simogo's Year Walk, which I also loved.

The presentation and interface are very minimal, a first-person adventure with a single-click interface (left click to advance and interact, and right click moves you backward) and mostly static backgrounds and sprites with simple paperdoll animation. The puzzles are pretty straightforward, with generous in-game hints to walk you through if you get stuck. This is a lovely example of a simple system used to very good effect. The gorgeous art is a real draw, with very nice music, including a couple of vocal pieces that feature in puzzles, and sound design that bring the evocative landscapes to life. 

Everything is grounded in Norse myth and history, with authentic runes, clothing, and decorative motifs. The voices in Old Norse (with subtitles) were a particularly nice touch. The game is just long enough to spend a few hours exploring and immersing yourself in this eerie, atmospheric, well realized world.

Si bien el título se me hizo algo corto, es muy divertido y ameno de jugar. La estética, los escenarios planteados y la banda sonora me parecieron espectaculares. La historia es interesante y te intriga lo suficiente como para seguir jugando. La mayoría de los puzles tienen un nivel de complejidad y desafío adecuados, aunque hay un par que son un poco rebuscados. La ambientación nórdica me encanta, y el desarrollo y conclusión de la trama me parecen bastante bien logrados.

Como dije, se me hizo un poco corto. Me habría gustado poder disfrutar más de este juegazo, pero no puedo dejar de admirar el empeño que los desarrolladores le pusieron a este juego: se nota que hicieron The Frostrune con mucho cariño y esfuerzo. El precio me parece adecuado en relación con el contenido y la calidad del título. Por supuesto que lo recomiendo.

Für die Spielzeit kann man ungefähr 2 - 3 Stunden einplanen, je nachdem wie sehr man sich in der Spielwelt verliert und wie gut man durch die Rätsel kommt. Auch muss man relativ viel Backtracken bzw. hin und her laufen für manche der Rätsel, aber das ist auch der einzige Kritikpunkt den ich an [i]The Frostrune[/i] habe. 

[u]Kaufempfehlung[/u]: Ich persönlich finde schon, dass das Spiel die 9,99€ wert ist, allerdings kann ich jeden verstehen, der das für die kurze Spieldauer nicht ausgeben möchte. 2,49€ ist der tiefste aufgezeichnete Preis, allerdings war [i]The Frostrune[/i] schon seit mindestens Juli 2022 nicht mehr im Sale.

It was also rather uncompelling plotwise; the protagonist was irrelevant to the story.

Some will enjoy it.  It depends what sort of puzzles you like solving.

Frostrune is an absolutely beautiful game. The art is stunning, and even though it's mostly static, it doesn't take away from its' beauty. It's also definitely not 6 hours, but that's what happens when you leave the game running to listen to the music. 

Speaking of which, music is very nice too, adding to the atmosphere. Your protagonist's remarks aren't voiced, but what few NPC dialogue and narration you encounter is and apparently recorded in Old Norse. Icing on the cake, really.

The Frostrune is an adventure game, sort of point&click, with a simple interface designed to work on mobiles as well. There are a few riddles, not particularly difficult if you've been paying attention to your surrondings while exploring. I think only one stumped me for a while, because frankly, I misunderstood what you were supposed to do, but other than that - no rubber ducky. Also, it's worth noting that should you ever get hopelessly stuck, there is a hint system that can basically guide you through the game. But it does pay off to not look there.

The story and length of the game are probably its' weakest points. Story because, well... it is pretty straightforward. You get a rough idea of what must have happened very early on and yup, that's what happened. No surprises there. You also aren't presented with any choices, but there are few additional things you can do. As for the length, according to the store page, Frostrune is finishable in 2 to 5 hours, taking away the time I had it just running in the background I did it in 3.5-4. So the gameplay time is on the shorter end of average for this genre. Could be longer though, I wouldn't mind.

To sum it up then!

PROS:
+ absolutely beautiful
+ nice music and voiceovers
+ have I mentioned how beautiful the art is?
+ well thought out riddles
+ solid story....

CONS:
- ...that isn't particularly surprising
- short

Would I recommend it? Absolutely, though considering the length of it, perhaps on a discounted price. Also, unless you missed some achievements, Frostrune isn't particularly replayable. No choices to change, no new paths to take. Like a beatiful comic book that you read once and remember fondly.

[i]The Frostrune[/i] is an elegant point-and-click adventure, with strong, authentic Norse culture. 

The story is set in and around an abandonned, coastal hamlet. The environment feels great. I used to live in Norway, and could see the familiar lighting and landscape features in the portrayal in the game). The hand-drawn art style is consistent and rich - a quick look at the trailer on the Steam Store page will give you a feel for it. The animations are simple, but very effective. Overall, I like it very much.

There is a story, but it is not a strong one. I see this game as more about the art, culture and puzzles than any deep narrative. However, it is dark. There are dead bodies of people and animals... plus there are supernatural elements. I wouldn't call it Scandinavian horror (for example, like [i]Year Walk[/i]), but it does have a grim side to it.

It is not a complicated game. I don't often play point-and-click games, and usually struggle when I do. I found this one manageable, and did not resort to a guide at any stage. It took me 7 hours on my playthrough and I got 15/20 of the achievements. The puzzles are not too complicated and the "hidden" objects to find are not obscure, but neither were they blatantly obvious either.

The interface is simple and clean and suits the style well. Having an in-game volume control would have helped, and the ability to save games would be nice. It does save the game between sessions, but you can't have more than one game going at a time, and if it crashes you need to start again.

The audio is excellent. The spoken parts are in Old Norse. The sound track is atmospheric and not too intrusive. The sound effects are good.

IRL I have done research on Nordic history and have given public lectures on the Norse Weltanschauung. I know some Old Norse language, but it's pretty rusty now. I could follow some of it, but I still relied on the Norwegian subtitles for the rest. (There are subtitles in other languages: German, English, etc..). I found the Norse language superb and it really added a lot. The use of runic script was also very good. I regard the game as being very faithful to our academic understanding of Norse culture, art and knowledge. This makes for a very refreshing change from the usual Hollywood-esque clichés that sadly permeate most modern titles on the subject. One detail that delighted me was the use of an iron block (not anvil!) in the blacksmith's hut.

In summary, if you like Nordic Dark Age life and beliefs, then I can strongly recommend this title. And I conclude this review by commending the developers on their exquisite attention to historical and cultural details. Well done!

All that is only diminished by the fact that the game is so very short. I beat the thing in just under 2 hours, and a decent chunk of that was just spent going back and forth on the map trying to remember 'wait, which fork took me to that one spot?'
It's a good game, I'd recommend anyone pick it up and play it, I don't think I would recommend buying it for the full $10 price. I'm sorry to the creator, again I can tell this was made with some real love, but it's simply too short to merit that.

Such a beautiful game; from the art to the music to the myths/legends, I just really enjoyed it all even when I got stuck trying to figure out the next step. It helps to take screenshots of stuff in case you can't memorize because then you can open your screenshots in the Steam overlay to look at the answers to the puzzles; or if you're like me, you just take screenshots of cool stuff in games and end up with the answers without necessarily trying.

I do wish there were an easier way to get around, such as a map where you can just click where you want to go instead of having to backtrack through each scene to get where you need to go (kind of like flipping back through the pages of a book to find that one sentence you need to re-read), but it's at least a pretty journey and changing scenes isn't exactly slow (it can just take several scene changes to get where you need to be). 

I'd say if you like puzzles and/or Norse myths and/or good art and/or good music then would probably enjoy this game. 

My hints: spacebar opens inventory (or click the pouch icon) and right-click backtracks through scenes (or you can left click near the arrow on the screen). I couldn't find a keybind for the seer's staff, which would be great if there was one but not a big deal that there isn't.

The Frostrune  is a short Myst-like game where you solve myth-based puzzles to defeat a Jotun who has killed a village. The blocky art fits the primitive atmosphere of a deserted Viking coastal village. The music and sound effects emphasize the setting. And the puzzles are intuitive with clues easy to find and a hint menu if you need it.

The dialogue is in some version of Norwegian with subtitles in the supported languages. As an English speaker, I enjoyed hearing the foreign dialogue to hear the similarities between that language and my own. I got to learn that apparently "frost" is a viking loan word.

Well worth your time if you enjoy puzzles and exploring the past or other cultures.
